replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistical technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a dataset while retaining as much variance as possible. To perform PCA, you first standardize the data. Next, you compute the covariance matrix. Then, you compute the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. You sort the eigenvalues in descending order and select the top k eigenvalues. You then form a matrix from the top k eigenvectors and use it to transform the original data into the new subspace. The mathematics of PCA can be complex, but it's not something to be anxious about. With practice and study, anyone can understand and apply PCA.
